title: NordVPN & ExpressVPN alternatives (UK, 2026)
buyer_question: Which VPN gives me real privacy, a usable free option, and no nasty renewal jump compared with NordVPN or ExpressVPN?
summary: Privacy-first comparison of five VPNs on price, renewal cost, logging audits and streaming. How to switch: buy the new VPN on its 30-day money-back window, test iPlayer/Netflix and speeds on your own devices, then turn off auto-renew on the old service before its renewal date (intro prices typically renew much higher). Prices approx, check current offer.

options.name: Proton VPN
options.price_uk: £0 free plan; Plus ~£2.39/mo on 2-yr plan (renews ~£67/yr) – approx, check current offer
options.price_us: $0 free plan; Plus ~$4.49/mo on 2-yr plan – approx, check current offer
options.billing: Unlimited-data free tier (1 device, no ads); Plus monthly, 1-yr or 2-yr; 30-day money-back; Proton Unlimited bundles Mail, Drive & Pass
options.best_for: Privacy-conscious users who want a genuinely free plan to start, Swiss jurisdiction, and open-source apps with independently audited no-logs policy
options.verdict: Top pick for privacy. Pros: only mainstream VPN with an unlimited-data free tier; Swiss-based; no-logs policy audited annually by Securitum since 2022; open-source, audited apps; Secure Core multi-hop; 10 devices on Plus; renewal price is lower than most rivals. Cons: free tier is 1 device with limited server choice and isn't meant for streaming; paid intro price slightly above Surfshark.

options.name: NordVPN
options.price_uk: ~£2.59–3.11/mo on 2-yr plan – approx, check current offer
options.price_us: ~$3.39–4.99/mo on 2-yr plan – approx, check current offer
options.billing: Basic / Plus / Complete tiers; 1-yr or 2-yr intro then higher renewal; 30-day money-back
options.best_for: People who want the most polished all-rounder for streaming and travel with minimal fiddling
options.verdict: Pros: fast NordLynx protocol, huge server network, reliable for iPlayer/Netflix, audited no-logs (Panama). Cons: aggressive upsells and renewal jump; 10-device cap; no free tier.

options.name: Surfshark
options.price_uk: ~£1.49–2.15/mo on 2-yr plan – approx, check current offer
options.price_us: ~$1.99–2.49/mo on 2-yr plan – approx, check current offer
options.billing: Starter / One / One+ tiers; long intro term + bonus months; 30-day money-back
options.best_for: Households and families with lots of devices on a tight budget
options.verdict: Pros: unlimited simultaneous devices, cheapest intro price, RAM-only servers, audited no-logs (Netherlands). Cons: renewal noticeably higher; owned by the same group as NordVPN, so not a true 'different company' switch.

options.name: Mullvad
options.billing: Flat monthly price, no contracts, no discounts or renewal hikes; pay by card, cash or crypto
options.best_for: Privacy purists who want anonymous accounts (no email needed) and honest flat pricing
options.verdict: Pros: account is just a random number, open-source apps, audited, Swedish, same price forever. Cons: dearer than long-term promos; only 5 devices; patchy for streaming; no money-back gimmicks or free tier.

options.name: ExpressVPN
options.price_uk: Basic ~£1.99/mo on 28-mo plan; ~£9.99 rolling monthly – approx, check current offer
options.price_us: Basic ~$2.79–4.99/mo on long plan; ~$12.99 monthly – approx, check current offer
options.billing: Basic / Advanced / Pro tiers since 2025; long intro term then much higher renewal; 30-day money-back
options.best_for: Existing users or less technical people who value very simple apps and strong streaming support
options.verdict: Pros: very easy apps, Lightway protocol, good streaming, audited TrustedServer RAM-only tech. Cons: renewal price jumps sharply; rolling monthly is among the most expensive; tiering now splits features across plans.
